orbisterrarum.spawnwait.title: Downloading the map around your spawn
orbisterrarum.spawnwait.text:
Orbis Terrarum is fetching OpenStreetMap data for %s.
%s of %s spawn regions ready · %s s elapsed.
The world will be created automatically as soon as the regions around the spawn are in.
orbisterrarum.spawnwait.hint: Each region is one request to the public Overpass servers (usually 5–40 s).
orbisterrarum.spawnwait.slow: The public Overpass servers are slow right now (this can take several minutes). Once downloaded, regions are cached on disk and never fetched again.
orbisterrarum.screen.noyacl.title: YetAnotherConfigLib is required
orbisterrarum.screen.noyacl.text: The Orbis Terrarum settings screens need the YetAnotherConfigLib mod (yet_another_config_lib_v3). Install it, or edit config/orbisterrarum/orbisterrarum.json by hand.
orbisterrarum.cat.location.desc: Where the world is, how big, and what it generates.
orbisterrarum.cat.location.intro: Open the World generator map to choose where the world is: search a place or coordinates, or right-click to put the spawn there (the spawn is the middle of the world, block 0, 0). Select an area there to pre-generate it or to keep the world inside it. The preset list gives the map a place to start from. Scale: 1 block = 1 m is real size, 2 is half size.
orbisterrarum.map.title: World map
orbisterrarum.map.search.hint: Find a place (Bryggen, Ulriken, an address)
orbisterrarum.map.help: Drag to move, scroll or double-click to zoom, right-click for marks, coordinates and (for operators) teleport. Press %s or Esc to close.
orbisterrarum.map.nodata: No map here: this world is not an Orbis Terrarum world, or the server does not run the mod (it tells the map where the world sits on Earth).
orbisterrarum.map.overworld: The map shows the overworld only.
orbisterrarum.map.blocks.tip: The Minecraft world seen from above (as on a map item) over the real map, to find buildings, villages and other structures. Click to change its opacity.
orbisterrarum.map.grey.tip: An orange haze over the chunks that are not generated yet (they generate when someone goes there).
orbisterrarum.map.zoomin: Zoom in to see the Minecraft map and what is generated.
orbisterrarum.mapcmd.noworld: This is not an Orbis Terrarum world.
orbisterrarum.mapcmd.started: Drawing the Minecraft map of %s regions in the background; /orbis map status shows progress.
orbisterrarum.mapcmd.progress: Drawing the Minecraft map: %s of %s regions done.
orbisterrarum.mapcmd.idle: The Minecraft map is up to date as far as it has been asked for; /orbis map render draws every region ahead of time.
orbisterrarum.mapcmd.done: The Minecraft map is drawn (%s regions).
orbisterrarum.opt.exactSpawn.desc: Everyone appears on exactly the spawn block (game rule respawn_radius 0). Off: Minecraft scatters new players up to 10 blocks around it.
orbisterrarum.preview.spawnset: Spawn set to %s: players start here, and it is the middle of the new world (block 0, 0).
orbisterrarum.opt.previewOpen.desc: Where the world is and what it generates, on a map: search a place or coordinates, right-click to set the spawn (the middle of the world), select the area to pre-generate (rectangle, ellipse, lasso, or a place or radius typed in) with its size, disk space and generation time, and switch pre-generation and the hard limit on or off. Without pre-generation the world generates around players as they go. Needs internet for the map and place searches.
orbisterrarum.preview.title: World generator map
orbisterrarum.preview.area.hint: Empty = city at the location; or a place, or km
orbisterrarum.preview.go.tip: Look up the area and show the chunks a pre-generation would make (Enter does the same).
orbisterrarum.preview.layer.tip: Map style: street map, satellite photos with place names, or elevation (heights in colour, with the height under the cursor).
orbisterrarum.preview.lower: World scale down: fewer metres per block (1:3 -> 1:2), a bigger, more detailed world with more chunks. This changes the world, not the map zoom (scroll to zoom). Also sets Metres per block, and the terrain detail to suit, on the Scale tab.
orbisterrarum.preview.higher: World scale up: more metres per block (1:2 -> 1:3), a smaller world with fewer chunks. This changes the world, not the map zoom (scroll to zoom). Also sets Metres per block, and the terrain detail to suit, on the Scale tab.
orbisterrarum.preview.browser.tip: The same preview as a web page, with more map layers and a place search.
orbisterrarum.preview.finding.here: Finding the area around the chosen location...
orbisterrarum.preview.counting: Found %s (%s km²). Working out its chunks...
orbisterrarum.preview.cubicReach: Cubic world: it reaches %s km from the spawn each way, and the shaded land lies beyond its border. A smaller scale (more metres a block) reaches farther.
orbisterrarum.preview.edge: Part of this lies past the world edge (30 million blocks from spawn): Minecraft cannot generate it. Use more metres per block or a spawn nearer to it.
orbisterrarum.preview.help: Hand: drag to move the map (right-drag does too, with any tool). Rectangle, ellipse, lasso: drag to select; Shift adds, Alt cuts out, Ctrl makes a square or circle, Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+D deselects. Scroll to zoom. Right-click sets the spawn point.
orbisterrarum.cat.scale.intro: How the real terrain becomes blocks. The defaults suit nearly every world. The world spans at most Y -2032 to 2031; a world height of 0 fits it to the place, which makes generating much faster.
orbisterrarum.cat.advanced.desc: World height, sea level, projection, terrain detail and how high mountains are handled.
orbisterrarum.cat.style.desc: The real sky, weather and seasons, and how buildings, roads and nature look.
orbisterrarum.cat.data.desc: Where the real-world data comes from. It downloads by itself as you explore, and a country's own services (sharper photos, rock map, road widths, lake surveys) are used wherever they cover. The last group needs a one-time import (see the README).
orbisterrarum.cat.data.sources: Imagery and elevation service addresses and coverage boxes are edited in config/orbisterrarum/orbisterrarum.json.
orbisterrarum.opt.realDaylight.desc: The sun rises and sets when it really does at the world's place (long summer days and long winter nights in the north), moving smoothly across the sky, and the moon shows its real phase. Sleeping does not skip a real night. Saved with the world.
orbisterrarum.opt.realWeather.desc: Clear skies, rain or thunderstorms as the Norwegian Meteorological Institute (yr / met.no) forecasts them for the coming hour where the players are. Whether it rains or snows is up to the biome, as in Minecraft. Saved with the world.
orbisterrarum.opt.realSeasons.desc: Grass and leaves take the colours of the real month: fresh green in spring, yellow, orange and brown through autumn, dull in winter; cold places get snow in winter, which melts in spring. Spruce and birch stay green. A new month shows the next time the world is opened. Saved with the world.
orbisterrarum.opt.realSnow.desc: Snow lies as deep as it really does today: Open-Meteo's weather models give the snow on the ground and the freezing level for every 25 km, and the snow deepens with height above the snow line, faster where winters are wet (last winter's precipitation there), so valleys stay green while the mountains are buried. New ground is laid with it; snow already in the world settles towards it a layer at a time and melts away when the real snow does. Checked every six hours. Off: snow follows the year-round climate. Saved with the world.
orbisterrarum.cat.performance.desc: How fast worlds generate and pre-generate on this computer.
orbisterrarum.cat.network.desc: Downloads: how many at once, how long to wait, what is kept in memory.
orbisterrarum.cat.overview.desc: The mod, its data folder, what you imported and your last pre-generations.
orbisterrarum.cat.storage.desc: Where the downloads are kept and how much each source takes.
orbisterrarum.overview.version: Orbis Terrarum %s for Minecraft %s. Worlds are set up in Create New World → Customize; these settings are the mod's own.
orbisterrarum.overview.disk: On disk: %s (Storage → Downloads by country has each source)
orbisterrarum.overview.disk.unknown: On disk: Storage → Downloads by country counts it
orbisterrarum.overview.noExtracts: No OpenStreetMap extracts (regions stream from Overpass). Import one with /orbis import <file.osm.pbf>.
orbisterrarum.opt.resetWorld.desc: Customize remembers the last world's settings. This puts every setting back to the mod's defaults (Bergen, 1:1, fitted height).
orbisterrarum.opt.resetWorld.ask: Put every setting of this screen back to the mod's defaults?
orbisterrarum.opt.preset.desc: Press Choose... for a list of well-known places (type to narrow it) and pick one: the world, and the World generator map, start there. A message confirms it.
orbisterrarum.opt.sourcesByCountry.desc: What every data source keeps on your disk, by country, the ones around your world first. Re-import data deletes a source's copies so they are downloaded again, fresh, when new chunks need them; Delete frees the space. Which sources a world uses is automatic: a country's own services wherever they cover, the worldwide data everywhere else.
orbisterrarum.sources.title: Data downloads by country
orbisterrarum.sources.note: Chunks already generated keep their data
orbisterrarum.sources.ask.reimport: Delete the %s kept from this source so it is downloaded again, fresh? The new copy comes the next time new chunks need it. Chunks already generated keep what they were built with.
orbisterrarum.sources.ask.free: Delete the %s kept from this source to free the space? It is downloaded again only if new chunks need it. Chunks already generated keep what they were built with.
orbisterrarum.sources.ask.delete: Delete these %s? Imported data only comes back by importing it again with its tool.
orbisterrarum.needs.title: Before generating
orbisterrarum.needs.checking: Checking whether it answers from your network...
orbisterrarum.needs.down: It does not answer from your network right now: new chunks will do without it.
orbisterrarum.opt.worldPreset.desc: Fills in every setting for a kind of world. City 1:1: one block per metre with real buildings, roads, caves and structures. Country map 1:32: one block per 32 m, terrain, water, glaciers, major roads and railways from the map, vanilla-scale towns on the real built-up areas, transverse Mercator projection, coarse elevation tiles; trees, ores, caves, structures and animals stay on for normal survival play -- a whole country in a few gigabytes, ready for Aternos. Import the country's OpenStreetMap extract first (/orbis import) so no Overpass requests are needed.
orbisterrarum.opt.projection.desc: Equirectangular is exact at city scale. Transverse Mercator keeps a whole country's shape and scale right (under 1 % error across Norway). Cannot be changed once the world exists.
orbisterrarum.opt.demZoom.desc: Detail of the Mapterhorn terrain tiles: 15 (~1.2 m per pixel at 60 N, 2.4 m at the equator) for 1:1 and 1:2 worlds, 16 where 1 m lidar exists and you want all of it, one less for each doubling of the scale beyond (1:4 14, 1:8 13, 1:16 12, 1:32 11), 9-10 for continents. Changing Metres per block sets this to suit; set it by hand after if you want. Higher zooms mean more and larger downloads.
orbisterrarum.opt.settlementBuildings.de: For worlds at 8 m per block or coarser, where a real house is smaller than a block: fills every built-up area of the map with vanilla-sized buildings -- houses with pitched roofs on residential land, 3-8 storey blocks on commercial and retail land, halls on industrial land -- so towns and cities are where they really are and as big as they really are. Every storey is lit. No effect on 1:1 worlds.
orbisterrarum.opt.villagerResidents.desc: Households in buildings: a bed on the ground floor (and one upstairs in taller buildings) with a villager per bed. They sleep, wander, flee and breed like a vanilla village. By default they are nitwits who never take a job, so trading stays something you find in real villages. At 1:32, each procedural house gets a bed and a villager.
orbisterrarum.opt.residentJobs.desc: Off (default): residents are nitwits and no workstations are placed, so the only traders are vanilla villages'. On: residents are ordinary villagers and buildings the map names as a business get the matching workstation (bakery -> smoker, library -> lectern, tailor -> loom, smithy -> smithing table, church -> bell, ...), so trades exist where real shops are.
orbisterrarum.opt.buildingSigns.desc: A sign beside every door with the building's real name from the map, or the kind of shop when it has no name. Navigate the city by its street names and shops.
orbisterrarum.opt.streetSigns.desc: A post with the street's real name at the corners of junctions, the sign along the street it names and readable from both sides. Wherever two differently named streets meet; at 1:2 or finer.
orbisterrarum.opt.furnishInteriors.desc: Furniture by building type: bookshelves and lecterns in libraries and schools, barrels and fish in fishmongers and markets, brewing stands in pharmacies, beds on every floor of hotels, tables and chairs in cafes and restaurants, pews and a bell in churches, shelves in shops and a loot chest in some of them. Entering buildings is worth it.
orbisterrarum.opt.streetLife.desc: Cats in residential streets, sheep and cows on meadows and farmland, a wandering trader on marketplaces, boats moored in marinas, gravestones in cemeteries (dark, so skeletons rise at night) and swings on playgrounds.
orbisterrarum.opt.transitLines.desc: Every railway, tram and light-rail line gets powered rails, connected curves and slopes, and a minecart waiting at each station with the station's name on a sign. Push the cart onto the line and ride the real network.
orbisterrarum.opt.landmarkAdvancements.d: On first start the world gets a datapack with one advancement per real landmark near the origin (peaks, viewpoints, castles, churches, museums, attractions) plus a grand tour for all of them. Delete the world's datapacks/orbis_landmarks folder to regenerate.
orbisterrarum.opt.tunnelLoot.desc: Every 128 m along a road tunnel, an alcove in the wall with a chest worth the fight: 12-24 iron, 2-5 diamonds in one chest out of four, lots of emeralds, gold, copper, lapis, redstone, experience, golden apples, torches, arrows and food, plus an enchanted iron (rarely diamond) tool or armour piece. Tunnels are unlit, so bring a torch.
orbisterrarum.opt.nvdbRoadWidths.desc: Source: the Norwegian Public Roads Administration's road database. Roads without a width on OpenStreetMap get their surveyed width and number of lanes. Norway only, at 1:1 and 1:2.
orbisterrarum.opt.externalPlaces.desc: Source: Overture Maps places. Shops, cafés, museums and clinics that OpenStreetMap misses get furniture and door signs. Import once: /orbis import-places <file.geojson>.
orbisterrarum.opt.treesFromCanopy.desc: Source: Meta and WRI's 1 m tree-height map of the world (or Kartverket's lidar in Norway when that is on). Trees stand where real trees stand, as tall as they are. Import once for your area: python tools/canopy_tiles.py. Without it, trees are scattered by land cover.
With lidar building heights on: gabled, hipped or flat roofs as the laser scan shows them, not guessed from the building type.
orbisterrarum.opt.residentsPerChunk.desc: Villagers per chunk on average, spread over the buildings of the chunk (a household is one or two of them). Villager AI is the most expensive thing a server runs: at simulation distance 12 the area around you is 625 chunks, so 0.3 is already about 190 villagers, six large vanilla villages' worth. 0.6 and up stutters on a laptop, on Aternos keep it at 0.2 or lower. Iron golems appear where ten or more live close together.
orbisterrarum.opt.majorRoadsOnly.desc: Only motorways, trunk, primary and secondary roads, railways and runways. For coarse maps, where every street would otherwise merge into one grey blob.
orbisterrarum.opt.metersPerBlock.desc: 1.0 is true 1:1. Larger values shrink the world (2 = half size) and make it generate faster. Press Enter after typing so the value is taken before you save.
orbisterrarum.opt.reliefKneeMeters.desc: Elevation below which the world is exactly 1:1 in Relative mode. 1500 m covers every coast and almost every city.
orbisterrarum.opt.reliefSmoothingKm.desc: Radius of the regional average that high terrain is lowered by. Larger keeps wider areas consistent but squeezes the highest peaks more.
orbisterrarum.opt.seaLevelY.desc: Block Y of real sea level. -1700 leaves 3731 blocks for mountains and 332 for the sea floor. Changing it requires a new world. Press Enter after typing so the value is taken before you save.
orbisterrarum.opt.highAltitudeWindow.des: When a new world's area has no sea within 30 km and lies high (mountains, plateaus), its 4,064 blocks are laid over the area's own ground instead of starting from sea level, so the mountains keep their true height: around Everest everything from Base Camp to the summit is 1:1, the Matterhorn and Mont Blanc too. Such a world has only a token sea: travel far enough and the lowlands flatten into a plain just above the world's floor, with a shallow sea beyond the coast. Turn this off for a mountain world meant to reach the real sea. Decided when the world is created.
orbisterrarum.opt.uniformHeights.desc: Every height in the world is scaled by the same amount, just enough for the highest ground of the world's area to fit under the ceiling: a Bergen world stays true 1:1, an Alps world comes out 1.3 times flatter, an Everest world 2.4 times, by the same amount everywhere, so every mountain keeps its true proportions to every other. Buildings, trees and players keep their real size. Mountains taller than the area's own are squeezed near the ceiling. Replaces Mountain worlds: true heights. Decided when the world is created.
orbisterrarum.opt.worldHeight.desc: 0 = fitted to the terrain around the origin when the world is created (a city 1000 m high gets a world about 1800 blocks tall instead of 4064, which makes every chunk about twice as cheap to generate, save and keep in memory). Or a fixed height, a multiple of 16 between 1024 and 4064; 4064 is the full Earth range. The floor (Y -2032) and sea level never move. Fixed once a world exists.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateBuildings.desc: Every OpenStreetMap building, extruded with its real colour, shape and roof.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateRoads.desc: Roads with markings and sidewalks, bridges, tunnels, railways, runways, piers.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateWater.desc: Sea from the coastline, lakes, rivers, canals, pools.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateLandCover.desc: Forests, farmland, parks, beaches, glaciers and other ground types.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateTrees.desc: Trees in forests, parks, gardens and where the aerial imagery shows canopy.
orbisterrarum.opt.roadGrading.desc: Roads are built the way real roads are: level across their width, following a smoothed line along the ground and meeting at the same height at junctions, cut into hillsides and raised over dips with earth banks beside them. Off: roads follow the ground column by column (tilted and stepped on steep slopes).
orbisterrarum.opt.roadRamps.desc: Where a paved road or pavement climbs a slope, each one-block step gets a half slab of the same surface, so hillside streets rise in walkable half steps instead of terraces; outdoor stairways get real stairs. On Minecraft 26.3 the slabs are concrete in the exact road colour; on older versions the closest-coloured slab.
orbisterrarum.opt.shopAwnings.desc: Striped or plain fabric awnings (wool slabs) over the doors of shops, cafés, restaurants and bars, above the name sign. Needs Minecraft 26.3 or later.
orbisterrarum.opt.autumnColours.desc: Autumn instead of summer. Birches and aspens turn yellow, oaks and other broadleaf trees yellow to red, about one tree in five still green. Broadleaf woods take the orange grass and foliage of Minecraft's autumn forest (with its foxes and rabbits), leaves lie in drifts under every broadleaf tree, some trees lie fallen with mushrooms on them, brown mushrooms come up, heath turns red. Grain fields are harvested with a few hay bales left, pumpkin patches ripen. Park lawns stay green. Needs Minecraft 26.3 or later (its poplar leaves and autumn forest); on older versions only the harvest, the fallen trees and the leaf drifts appear.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateStreetFurnitur: Street lamps, traffic lights, crossings, benches, fountains, fences, walls, power lines.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateSchematics.des: Hand-built .schem/.nbt models from config/orbisterrarum/schematics placed at their real coordinates.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateBedrock.desc: A bedrock layer at the bottom of the world.
orbisterrarum.opt.generateOres.desc: Coal, iron, copper, gold, redstone, lapis, diamond and emerald veins, placed by depth below the real surface so mining works anywhere on Earth.
orbisterrarum.opt.spawnAnimals.desc: Spawn animals when chunks generate, using vanilla's rules (grass, daylight). Monsters spawn in the dark as usual.
orbisterrarum.opt.vanillaStructures.desc: Mineshafts, strongholds, ancient cities and trial chambers are sunk 100 blocks below the local ground with their vanilla depths kept, so the End is reachable. Villages, temples, outposts, ruined portals, shipwrecks and monuments appear only where the map has no buildings, roads or water.
orbisterrarum.opt.vanillaCaves.desc: Vanilla-style cave tunnels with lava at the bottom, dungeons (mob spawner rooms with chests), amethyst geodes, fossils, water and lava springs and glow lichen, all in the underground band 100 blocks below the local ground. Never opens into streets or under buildings.
orbisterrarum.opt.interiorLights.desc: A sea lantern in every sixth floor block of hollow buildings, so nothing spawns indoors and the mob cap is not used up inside a city.
orbisterrarum.opt.streetLights.desc: Lamp posts every 24 m along lit and urban streets in addition to the mapped ones. Parks, forests and yards stay dark, as in real life.
orbisterrarum.opt.hollowBuildings.desc: Buildings get floors per storey instead of being solid.
orbisterrarum.opt.buildingDoors.desc: A door on the street side of each building.
orbisterrarum.opt.metersPerStorey.desc: How tall one floor is in real metres, for buildings the map only gives a number of floors (or nothing): a four-storey house at 3 m is 12 m tall, scaled like every other building (6 blocks at 1:2). Inside, floors are always this many blocks apart so they can be walked; grand buildings (churches, museums, palaces) get at least 4.
orbisterrarum.opt.roadCenterLineColour.d: Norway and most of Europe: white or yellow; USA: yellow.
orbisterrarum.opt.roadSidewalks.desc: Automatic sidewalks on residential and larger streets.
orbisterrarum.opt.seaFromElevation.desc: Where there is no coastline data, columns below sea level become ocean.
orbisterrarum.opt.treeDensityForest.desc: Trees per column inside forests. 0.045 is one tree per 4.7 × 4.7 m.
orbisterrarum.opt.climateOverride.desc: Auto uses latitude and elevation. Force arid for deserts or humid for jungles where the estimate is wrong.
orbisterrarum.opt.temperatureOffsetC.des: Added to the estimated mean temperature: +3 for Gulf-Stream coasts, -3 for continental interiors.
orbisterrarum.opt.snowTemperatureC.desc: Mean annual temperature below which ground is snow-covered and water frozen.
orbisterrarum.opt.snowAtHighElevation.de: Snow caps above the local snow line.
orbisterrarum.opt.realWaterDepths.desc: Sources: a country's lake surveys where Orbis knows one (Norway's NVE, see Sources by country) and, if you imported them, GLOBathy lake depths for the rest of the world (python tools/lake_depths.py). Lakes deepen away from the shore instead of having a flat bottom; surveyed lakes get their measured bed. Rivers are as deep as their width suggests.
orbisterrarum.opt.bedrockTypes.desc: Sources: the Geological Survey of Norway's bedrock map in Norway, Macrostrat's geological map of the world everywhere else. The stone underground, in cliffs and on bare rock is the real rock: granite, diorite, gabbro (deepslate), basalt, schist (tuff), limestone and marble (calcite), sandstone, with gneiss and loose ground as plain stone. Ores form in all of them. How detailed it is depends on the place: down to single hills in Norway, much of Europe, North America and Australia; whole regions in parts of Asia and Africa.
orbisterrarum.opt.lidarSurfaceModel.desc: Source: Kartverket's laser-scanned surface model. Buildings without a height on OpenStreetMap get their measured height and roof shape instead of an estimate. Off: used by itself whenever Kartverket answers from your network (new worlds), skipped when it doesn't. On: always asked, with a check before generating (a VPN to Norway helps on networks it doesn't answer). What it downloads is kept. Only used up to 1:4 (4 m per block).
orbisterrarum.opt.useAerialImagery.desc: Source: Esri World Imagery, satellite and aerial photos of the whole world. Roofs, lawns, pavement and bare ground take the colour they have in the photos where OpenStreetMap has no detail.
orbisterrarum.opt.useHighResElevation.de: Source: Kartverket (Norway) and USGS 3DEP (USA) terrain services. Usually leave this off: the normal terrain source (Mapterhorn) already carries the same laser-scanned terrain, and these services are slow. Only used up to 1:4 (4 m per block): coarser scales skip it, and choosing one switches it off.
orbisterrarum.opt.useBathymetry.desc: Source: Open Waters Seascape, the GEBCO world ocean map with regional surveys. Fjords, harbours and the open sea get their real depth, down to 300 m.
orbisterrarum.opt.atlasBuildingHeights.d: Source: GlobalBuildingAtlas (Technical University of Munich), a height for every building on Earth estimated from satellites. Buildings without a height on OpenStreetMap use it. Import once for your area: python tools/gba_heights.py.
orbisterrarum.opt.worldCoverLandCover.de: Source: ESA WorldCover, a 10 m satellite map of the whole world. Where OpenStreetMap does not say what covers the ground, this decides: forest, grass, fields, rock, wetland or snow.
orbisterrarum.opt.imageryZoom.desc: 18 is 0.6 m per pixel at the equator; 19 is sharper but downloads four times as many tiles.
orbisterrarum.opt.imageryRoofColours.des: Untagged buildings get the median orthophoto colour of their roof.
orbisterrarum.opt.imageryGroundClassific: Lawn, pavement, soil, sand, rock and snow where OpenStreetMap only has zoning.
orbisterrarum.opt.imageryTreeCover.desc: Plant trees where the imagery shows canopy, even outside mapped forests.
orbisterrarum.opt.buildingHeightsFromSur: Where a lidar surface model covers a building without height tags, measure its real height.
orbisterrarum.opt.waitForOsm.desc: Chunks wait until their OpenStreetMap region has downloaded. Off: chunks whose data is not yet there generate as terrain only.
orbisterrarum.opt.prefetchSpawnAtStartup: Download the spawn regions while you are still in the menu so the first world creates instantly.
orbisterrarum.map.select.ceiling: Peaks here reach Y %s; this world ends at Y %s
orbisterrarum.map.select.ceiling2: their tops get squeezed by up to %s blocks
orbisterrarum.opt.fastPregen.desc: Orbis builds the ground, water, roads, buildings and caves of the chunks ahead of a pre-generation itself, on half the processor cores, and Minecraft only adds decoration, light and animals. Several times faster. Chunks that already exist are never touched.
orbisterrarum.opt.fastPregenThreads.desc: How many processor threads build terrain ahead of a pre-generation. Auto uses half of them; more can be faster, but Minecraft's own threads (decoration, light, saving) need the rest. Takes effect at the next pre-generation.
orbisterrarum.opt.parallelChunkCompressi: In Orbis worlds, chunks are compressed for saving on several threads instead of Minecraft's one disk thread, so saving keeps up with fast pre-generation. The files are the same as Minecraft's own.
orbisterrarum.opt.pregenPauseWorld.desc: While a pre-generation runs the world stands still, like /tick freeze: mobs, crops, redstone, time and weather. Chunks keep generating and you can still move around. The time the game spent on the world goes to generating instead. Everything carries on when the pre-generation ends or stops.
orbisterrarum.opt.fastChunkWrites.desc: Orbis worlds save chunks without waiting for the disk after each one (Minecraft's "Sync chunk writes" off for them only; other worlds keep your game setting). Much faster pre-generation and fewer freezes while saving. After a power cut or crash the last few seconds of chunks may be lost; they simply generate again. Takes effect the next time a world opens.
orbisterrarum.opt.regionPrefetchRadius.d: Rings of 512 m regions kept downloading around each player.
orbisterrarum.opt.regionCacheSize.desc: Decoded regions kept in memory. Each is about 6 MB; lower this on small servers.
orbisterrarum.opt.overpassConcurrentRequ: Overpass requests in flight at once. Public servers rate-limit per IP; 4 is safe, 8 only when self-hosting.
orbisterrarum.opt.osmMaxWaitMinutes.desc: How long a chunk waits for its region before generating terrain only.
orbisterrarum.opt.demTileCacheSize.desc: Elevation tiles kept in memory (about 256 KB each).
orbisterrarum.opt.imageryTileCacheSize.d: Orthophoto tiles kept in memory (about 256 KB each).
orbisterrarum.opt.debugLogging.desc: Log every region download and rasterisation.
orbisterrarum.map.markers.tip: Size of the arrows, the spawn marker and the pins on the map.
orbisterrarum.group.data.auto.desc: Fetched as you explore and kept on your disk; nothing to do.
orbisterrarum.group.data.lidar.desc: Measured building heights and roof shapes from national laser scans are used by themselves where they exist: Switzerland, the Netherlands, France, North Rhine-Westphalia, Estonia, Czechia, Canada (where it has been scanned), Oregon, Kentucky and Washington DC (at 1:4 or finer). Where no tree map is imported, trees there get their measured height too. Norway's Kartverket service cannot be reached from every network (outside Norway you may need a VPN) and is slow, so it is off unless you switch it on; creating a world then tells you whether it answers from your network.
orbisterrarum.group.data.import.desc: These read data you download once for your area with the tools described in the README. They do nothing until you have.
orbisterrarum.opt.dataFolder.desc: The folder the mod keeps its downloads and imports in (terrain, photos, map data, country extracts, lidar, lake and rock data, map tiles). Shown here is the folder in use. Pick another with Choose folder, then press Move downloads to carry everything there (or Save to start the new folder empty). The settings file, landmarks and map marks stay in the config folder.
orbisterrarum.opt.villagerClockHours.des: With real daylight on: villagers live by the town's real local time, as people do: up at 07:00, at work 08:00 to 16:00, meeting in the village until 18:00, in bed at 22:00, whatever the sun is doing (in a northern winter they go to work in the dark). Off: they follow the sun, working from about two hours after sunrise and sleeping from sunset. The time zone is looked up once per world (Open-Meteo).
orbisterrarum.group.storage.desc: Where the downloaded and imported data is kept on your disk. It can grow to many gigabytes, so it can live on another drive.
orbisterrarum.opt.chooseFolder.desc: Opens your system's folder dialog. The folder you pick is used once you press Save.
orbisterrarum.opt.openFolder.desc: Shows the data folder in your file manager, for example to move old downloads into it.
orbisterrarum.toast.nofolder.desc: The dialog was closed, or none could be opened on this system: type the path instead.
orbisterrarum.opt.moveData.desc: Moves everything the mod has downloaded or imported (terrain, photos, map data, country extracts, lidar, map tiles...) from the folder in use now to the folder above, and switches to it. Between drives this copies each file and then deletes the original, so it frees the old drive as it goes; files the new folder already has are kept. Only from the main menu (not while a world is open). It can take several minutes for many gigabytes: a progress bar shows how far it has got.
orbisterrarum.toast.move.inworld.desc: The mod reads these files while a world is open. Move them from the main menu (Mod Menu).
orbisterrarum.toast.move.same.desc: That is already the folder in use. Choose another folder first.
orbisterrarum.map.select.tip: Select area: pick part of the map to pre-generate, as in an image editor. Shift adds, Alt cuts out, Ctrl makes a square or circle, Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+D deselects. While selecting, right-drag (or middle-drag, or Space + drag) moves the map.
orbisterrarum.map.select.lasso.tip: Lasso: drag to draw freehand, or click corner after corner and close with a double-click, the first corner or Enter (Backspace removes a corner, Escape cancels).
orbisterrarum.map.select.mode.tip: Mode: %s. New replaces the selection, Add joins it, Subtract cuts it out (click to change). Holding Shift adds and Alt cuts out for one shape.
orbisterrarum.map.select.generate.tip: Pre-generate the selected chunks on the server, north to south, sea included. Progress appears in chat every 30 s; /orbis pregen stop ends it, and pressing Generate again with the same selection resumes.
orbisterrarum.map.select.help: Drag a rectangle or ellipse, or draw with the lasso. Shift adds, Alt cuts out, Ctrl makes a square or circle. Right-drag moves the map.
orbisterrarum.map.select.polygon: Click corner after corner; double-click, click the first corner or press Enter to close. Backspace removes a corner, Escape cancels.
orbisterrarum.map.select.size: about %s on disk, about %s to generate
orbisterrarum.map.select.sent: Sent to the server: progress appears in chat.
orbisterrarum.map.select.rect.tip: Rectangle: drag from corner to corner (hold Ctrl for a square).
orbisterrarum.map.select.ellipse.tip: Ellipse: drag across it (hold Ctrl for a circle).
orbisterrarum.map.hardlimit: Outside the hard limit: never generates
orbisterrarum.map.select.expand.tip: Expand selection (hold Ctrl for a small step)
orbisterrarum.map.select.shrink.tip: Shrink selection (hold Ctrl for a small step)
orbisterrarum.map.select.sea.off: Skip open sea: off (the area is generated sea and all)
orbisterrarum.map.select.sea.on: Skip open sea: on (deep sea is left out and generates when someone sails there)
orbisterrarum.map.select.toosmall: Too small to shrink any further.
orbisterrarum.preview.find.hint: A place, coordinates or a radius (5 km)
orbisterrarum.preview.findgo.tip: Adds the place's outline to the selection (or cuts it out, or replaces it, as the mode button on the left says), and moves the spawn there if it was elsewhere. A place without an outline (a summit, a building, an address) or coordinates (60.39, 5.32) moves the spawn and the map there. A number of km is a radius around the spawn.
orbisterrarum.preview.start: Search a place at the top, or right-click to put the spawn there. To pre-generate, pick a tool on the left and draw the area, or type a place or a radius.
orbisterrarum.preview.none.how: Select the area the new world will generate: draw it with the rectangle, ellipse or lasso on the left, or type a place (Bergen) or a radius (5 km) at the top and press Select. Its size, disk space and time show here.
orbisterrarum.preview.generate.tip: ON: the new world generates the selection by itself when it first opens, and carries on each time it opens until it is done. OFF: it generates around players as they go.
orbisterrarum.preview.generate.note.on: The new world will generate this selection by itself when it opens.
orbisterrarum.preview.generate.note.off: Switch "Generate on creation" on (below) and the new world generates this selection by itself.
orbisterrarum.map.select.hand.tip: Hand: drag to move the map (right-drag or middle-drag move it with any tool).
orbisterrarum.opt.pregenSkipOpenSea.desc: The /orbis pregen commands (a place's area, a radius) leave out chunks that are deep sea all over (deeper than 40 m everywhere): a smaller world to upload and a shorter sweep, and those chunks generate quickly when someone sails there. Off: everything is generated, sea included. Areas drawn on the map have their own Skip open sea button. Saved with the world.
orbisterrarum.preview.limit.tip: ON (hard limit): nothing outside the selection ever generates, even if players go there; an invisible wall along its edge keeps them in. Areas pre-generated later join it.
orbisterrarum.preview.limit.note: Hard limit: nothing outside this selection will generate, and an invisible wall keeps players inside.
orbisterrarum.preview.foundmoved: %s selected (%s km²). The spawn moved there.
orbisterrarum.preview.pointfound: %s (%s): the spawn is there now. It is a place, not an area, so nothing was selected; draw an area or type a radius (5 km) to select around it.
orbisterrarum.mapdata.title: Map data for this world
orbisterrarum.mapdata.looking: Looking for a map data file for this place...
orbisterrarum.mapdata.offer:
This place's map (roads, buildings, water) can come from your disk instead of the online map servers, which are slow and sometimes overloaded.

Download OpenStreetMap's file for %s from Geofabrik (%s) and keep only this world's area (tens of MB)? It downloads in the background while the world opens; the world uses the online servers until it is ready, and the big file is deleted afterwards.
orbisterrarum.opt.offerMapDownloads.desc: When you create a world and no map data on your disk covers its area, offer OpenStreetMap's file for that place from Geofabrik (the smallest region that holds the area, with its size). Only the world's area is kept, so generation reads the map from your disk instead of the online servers. Off: the online servers, as before.
orbisterrarum.opt.keepDownloadedMapFiles: Keep Geofabrik's country file after the world's area is imported (in extracts-src), so another world in the same country needs no new download. Off: deleted, which saves gigabytes.
orbisterrarum.opt.buildingHeights.desc: Walkable floors: every storey is 3 blocks at any scale, so buildings look right beside you and you can walk their floors; they are taller than their footprint at 1:2. True to scale: heights shrink with the scale like everything else (a 4-storey house is 6 blocks at 1:2, 3 at 1:4). Auto: walkable at 1:2 and finer, true to scale coarser.
orbisterrarum.map.night.tip: Day or night street map: the sun is the normal map, the moon the dark one. Click to switch.
orbisterrarum.opt.farViewFromData: Distant Horizons: land not generated yet
orbisterrarum.opt.farViewFromData.desc: With Distant Horizons installed, its far view also shows land nobody has generated yet, painted from the world's data (elevation, climate, snow) the way the world will be generated. Off: only generated chunks appear in it.
orbisterrarum.opt.voxyFarView.desc: With Voxy installed, in singleplayer: fills Voxy's far view around you with the world's saved chunks, and where nothing is generated yet (also past the world's border) with land painted from the world's data. The first fill of a world takes a while and works your processor hard; it is remembered, so later visits only add what is new. Switching this off stops the filling, but what Voxy already holds stays on screen: Voxy keeps it with the world. To hide it use Voxy's own switch; to clear it, delete the voxy folder in the world's folder.
orbisterrarum.opt.voxyFarViewChunks.desc: How far around you the Voxy far view is filled, in chunks (1,024 chunks is 16 km of blocks).
